title: Karnaugh maps 1: start with four squares
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Write −13 as an 8-bit two’s-complement integer .
questions.feedback: Start with +13 = 00001101. Invert the bits → 11110010, then add 1 → 11110011.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: For the circuit shown, simplify Q = ¬(A ∨ B) using De Morgan’s Law.
questions.feedback: NOT of an OR becomes AND of the individually negated inputs. Both expressions are equivalent.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Complete one full left-to-right pass of ascending bubble sort. What is the resulting array?
questions.feedback: Compare neighbouring items and swap where needed: [4,9,6,2,8] → [4,6,9,2,8] → [4,6,2,9,8] → [4,6,2,8,9].

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Normalise this positive binary mantissa without changing its value. Give the new exponent.
questions.feedback: Shift the mantissa point two places right (0.001101 → 0.110100), so decrease the exponent from 4 to 2. The numerical value stays the same.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: Karnaugh map — A grid used to simplify the outputs from a truth table.
Group — Adjacent 1s circled as one rectangular region.
Adjacent — Cells next to each other horizontally or vertically.
Simplify — Express the same output with fewer Boolean variables.
Gray code — An ordering in which neighbouring labels differ by one bit.

blocks.title: Map the truth-table outputs
blocks.text: For each combination of A and B, find the same output Q in the map. The grid moves outputs; it does not change them.

blocks.title: Group adjacent 1s
blocks.text: Circle the two 1s in the bottom row. A group can contain 1, 2, 4, 8… adjacent 1s. Use the largest useful group.

blocks.title: Compare the input values
blocks.text: For the two circled cells: A stays 1; B changes from 0 to 1.

blocks.title: Keep only what stays the same
blocks.text: Look at each input variable across the grouped cells (where Q = 1): In our group, A = 1 in both cells, while B changes. Keep A, leave out B: Q = A .

blocks.title: Worked example · How does this four-square map simplify?
blocks.text: Use the Boolean input labels and large output values to group the 1s and derive Q.
